reason: Doc-link checker for the detector defects in #686: module-size 28319->28616 (+297). Measured on this tree branched from dced1f1, and attributed empirically rather than arithmetically -- moving scripts/check_doc_links.mjs aside and re-running `harness check-arch --json` drops metricRegressions to null, i.e. to exactly main's allowed 28319 from #504's allowance. So the whole +297 is that one new file and nothing else in the change contributes: the two test files (ts/test/doc-links.test.ts, ts/test/doc-links-testkit.ts) are test code and module-size does not count them, and the rest of the diff is CHANGELOG.md, ADR 0012, five repaired links, and two entryPoints entries. The file is a dead-link checker that harness's own checkStructureDrift cannot be, on this repo: all 27 of its structural drift findings are detector defects (fence-blind link extraction, and a slugifyHeading that trims before it hyphenates), filed upstream as Intense-Visions/harness-engineering#1342. Of the 297 lines, roughly 120 are comment and doc block, deliberately: the file duplicates a capability the toolchain claims to provide, and a reader who does not know why will delete it or, worse, will reach for the entropy.drift.docPaths allowlist this file exists to avoid. The remainder is four small functions that each encode one defect -- blankFencedLines (a fence closes only on a bare fence at least as long as the opener, so ```` legitimately wraps ```), slugify (no trim, one hyphen per whitespace character, \p{L}\p{N} rather than ASCII \w), headingSlugs (GitHub's -1/-2 duplicate suffixes, fences excluded), extractLinks (inline AND reference-style definitions) -- plus the walk, the generator-stamp branch, and the exit-code contract. Nothing was absorbed here to avoid a fix: newViolations is 0 and the pre-existing violations stay at 21. Nor is this a case where splitting would help -- module-size is a repo-wide aggregate, so four files summing to 297 lines would score identically to one, and the file is 297 lines total, well under the per-file thresholds. Earning its keep on arrival: the checker found five genuinely dead links that #676 missed (three docs/adr/ targets orphaned by the move to docs/knowledge/decisions/, two docs/wiki/ links to agents/skills/ missing a path segment), all reference-style definitions, a form the upstream detector does not read at all. REBASED 2026-08-12: the recorded absolute was 28616, measured when this branch was cut from dced1f1. #695 (naming-craft polish) then merged with its own +18 allowance, moving main's allowed total to 28634. This file's own contribution is unchanged at +297 -- only the absolute base moved beneath it. That coupling is the known hazard of absolute-valued allowances: every allowance merged after a branch is cut silently invalidates that branch's recorded number, which is why the arrow in a check-arch verdict must never be read as a delta (#689).
